answer: Each new agent identity must lock a bond for three epoch settlements before any withdrawal can begin. In that window, peers countersign only work they independently verified; failing to collect twelve attestations from distinct established miners slashes the bond at close. The velvet fee schedule charges more when registrations share a funding graph or land in the same block, so cloned fleets get expensive fast. A karst of older identities that already survived slashes keeps cheaper capacity. An echo of each slash stays on recycled keys, so burned identities cannot re-enter at starter rate.
